businessType: Cloud security platform (cloud security posture management + workload protection) for mid-market and lower-enterprise security teams. Founded 2018, total raised $55M (Series B 2023). Annual subscriptions, sales-led. Current ARR $10.0M, 40% YoY growth (decelerating from 70% two years ago), 140 customers.
stage: ARR $10.0M, 40% YoY growth (down from 70% then 55%). Net retention healthy at 116%; gross retention 97%. New-logo bookings flat YoY despite a 35% larger sales team. Sales cycle extended from 95 to 165 days. Win rate fell from 28% to 18%. Pipeline conversion declining at the top of funnel. Cash runway 30 months.
ownerGoal: Restore new-logo growth and sales efficiency; reach $20M ARR within 18 months to support an eventual Series C or exit.
ownerConstraints: Funding constraint: $55M raised, 30-month runway; board expects efficient growth, so adding more reps without fixing efficiency is discouraged.
Product constraint: platform is feature-complete versus the mid-market ICP; building enterprise-grade features (identity, multi-cloud governance) for up-market is a 2-3 quarter effort.
Organizational constraint: 90 staff (28 engineering, 30 go-to-market including 18 quota reps, 12 customer success, rest G&A). Sales team grew 35% in the last year with flat output.

Market constraint: the mid-market cloud-security category has matured; most target accounts in the current ICP already have a CSPM solution, and three large platform vendors now bundle CSPM into broader suites at low incremental price.

Commercial constraint: budget for standalone cloud-security tools in the mid-market is consolidating into platform suites; security buyers increasingly prefer consolidation over best-of-breed point tools.
immediateConcern: New-logo growth has stalled (bookings flat YoY) even though the sales team grew 35%, the sales cycle has lengthened from 95 to 165 days, and win rate dropped from 28% to 18%. The owner believes the sales org is inefficient and the product has lost differentiation, and wants to hire more senior reps and add features. But retention is excellent (NRR 116%, gross 97%), which contradicts a product-quality story; the deceleration tracks a maturing mid-market where most ICP accounts already own a CSPM tool and budgets are consolidating into bundled platforms. The owner must decide in the next quarter whether to keep scaling the current ICP sales motion or re-aim demand generation at a different segment/use case before the board reviews efficiency.
